text: Then Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests set to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set its doors in place, and they consecrated the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred, all the way to the Tower of Hananel.
Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri.
The Fish Gate was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah. They laid its beams and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs, and next to them Zadok son of Baana.

Next to them the men of Tekoa made repairs, but their nobles would not put their shoulders to the work of their Lord.[fn: The Hebrew word can mean either their Lord (God) or their lords, that is, their supervisors.]

versions.text: Next to them the men of Tekoa made repairs, but their nobles would not put their shoulders to the work of their Lord.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew אֲדֹנֵיהֶם is plural in form and is legitimately read either as a reference to God or to the human overseers of the work. Capitalizing 'Lord' fixes one interpretation; a short footnote preserves the ambiguity for the reader without changing the reading text.

text: The Old Gate was repaired by Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah. They laid its beams and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
Next to them Melatiah of Gibeon and Jadon of Meronoth made repairs, along with the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, which was under the authority of the governor of the province Beyond the River.
Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith, made repairs, and next to him Hananiah, a perfumer. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his own house, and next to him Hattush son of Hashabniah.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section, along with the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of the other half of the district of Jerusalem, made repairs, he and his daughters.

The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the residents of Zanoah. They rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place, and they repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.[fn: About 450 metres or 1,500 feet.]

versions.text: The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the residents of Zanoah. They rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place, and they repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.
versions.explanation: An ancient measure is left unexplained. A brief footnote giving the modern equivalent helps hearers grasp the size of the section repaired; the reading text itself is unchanged.

text: The Dung Gate was repaired by Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem. He rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.

The Fountain Gate was repaired by Shallun son of Col-Hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah. He rebuilt it, roofed it over, and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the pool that was made and the House of the Warriors.

versions.text: Beyond him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the reservoir and the House of the Warriors.
versions.explanation: 'Beyond him' reads oddly in a list of successive workers; 'After him' matches אַחֲרָיו and flows better when read aloud. 'The pool that was made' (הַבְּרֵכָה הָעֲשׂוּיָה) is also closer to the Hebrew than the modern-sounding 'reservoir'.

text: Next to him the Levites made repairs under Rehum son of Bani. Beside him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his own district.

Next to him their fellow Levites made repairs under Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.[fn: The Hebrew text reads Bavvai here; he is probably the same man called Binnui in verse 24.]

versions.text: Next to him their fellow Levites made repairs under Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew of this verse has Bavvai, not Binnui. Harmonizing with verse 24 is defensible, but the reader should be told that the name in the Hebrew text differs.

text: Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, from a point facing the ascent to the armory as far as the angle in the wall.
Next to him Baruch son of Zabbai worked with zeal, repairing another section from the angle to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
Next to him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the entrance of Eliashib's house to the far end of it.
Next to him the priests from the surrounding countryside made repairs.
Next to them Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their house, and next to them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
Next to him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner,
and Palal son of Uzai worked opposite the angle and the tower projecting from the upper palace of the king, beside the court of the guard. Next to him was Pedaiah son of Parosh.
The temple servants were living on Ophel, and they made repairs up to a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.

versions.text: The temple servants living on Ophel made repairs up to a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew states as a fact that the temple servants were living on Ophel (הָיוּ יֹשְׁבִים), with the repair work supplied from context. The revision keeps the necessary implied verb while preserving the main clause of the Hebrew sentence.

text: Next to them the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from the great projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each in front of his own house.
Next to them Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house, and next to him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate.
Next to him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his living quarters.
Next to him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and on to the upper room at the corner.
And between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he flew into a rage and, seething with anger, ridiculed the Jews.

In the presence of his associates and the army of Samaria he said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore things for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring stones back to life out of heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"

versions.text: In the presence of his associates and the army of Samaria he said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Do they think they can restore the wall? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring stones back to life out of heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew clause is obscure and does not name an object; supplying "the wall" narrows an intentionally general taunt. A more open rendering keeps the ambiguity of the original, and a footnote noting the difficulty of the Hebrew could be helpful.

text: Tobiah the Ammonite, standing beside him, said, "Whatever they build—if even a fox climbed up on it, it would break down their wall of stones!"
Hear us, our God, for we are despised. Turn their taunts back on their own heads, and hand them over as plunder in a land of captivity.
Do not cover over their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before you, for they have provoked you to anger in the presence of the builders.

versions.text: Do not cover over their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before you, for they have hurled insults in the face of the builders.
versions.explanation: The verb הִכְעִיסוּ ("they provoked to anger") normally has God as its implied object; לְנֶגֶד הַבּוֹנִים indicates the setting ("before/in front of the builders"), not the target of the insult. The current rendering makes the builders the object of the offense and loses the appeal to God's own honor, which is the basis of the prayer.

text: So we rebuilt the wall, and it was joined together all the way around to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.

versions.text: So we rebuilt the wall, and it was joined together all the way around to half its height, for the people worked with all their heart.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew idiom describes the people's willing mind or resolve to work, which is the reason the wall progressed; "worked with all their heart" adds "all" and shifts the sense from disposition to intensity of labor.
